<description>
`FlushStateToDisk()` returns `state.Error(...)` when `FlushChainstateBlockFile()` fails, relying on the invariant that the flush-error notification has already been emitted (so the node is aborted). Today that invariant holds only because every `success = false` branch in `FlushBlockFile`/`FlushUndoFile` happens to call `flushError()` itself. A future flush source, or a new error branch, that fails without notifying would make `FlushStateToDisk()` report an error without `AbortNode()` being triggered.

This PR makes that invariant hold by construction: whenever a flush reports failure, the flush-error notification has been emitted.

- **test: cover FlushBlockFile flush-error notifications**: `BlockManager` unit tests that inject a failure on the block file and on the undo file separately, and assert that each failure emits `flushError`.
- **blockstorage: encapsulate flush+notify in FlushFile**: a single `FlushFile()` helper performs the flush and emits the notification on failure; `FlushBlockFile` and `FlushUndoFile` delegate to it. No behaviour change.

Follow-up to #35714. Possible further work on flush error handling is listed in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35714#pullrequestreview-5697890316 (pruned-file deletion after a failed flush is handled in #36735).
</description>
